sentences.text: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage The 2026 Conservative conference is big enough to justify using Birmingham's Symphony Hall as its main stage again.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: So, Kemi Badenoch will tread the same stage ageing rockers Marillion took last month - and where sequinned soprano Katherine Jenkins will perform next week.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: She'll also avoid the humiliation of a national party leader being squashed into a side room at a corporate conference centre (with drapes portioning off the empty space).
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Simply, the party is able to put bums on seats again - and by that measure, things are looking up.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Badenoch goes into the conference with her own position secure in the party.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: One senior Tory says "she has actually defied cynics like me" who initially disapproved of her leadership.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Her standing with the public has improved and she is now, again on a very simple but crucial measure, much better known.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: The shadow of the years of chaos still looms.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: And while Badenoch has made good progress since she took the job, most of that was up against an unpopular prime minister, Sir Keir Starmer, on whom she landed plenty of political punches.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: She has to show "what being Conservative is now", says another senior Tory, taking on a different, more popular, rival in Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: The Tories' warm-up to conference has been so far, so traditional.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: A proposed dramatic expansion of prison places kicks off Badenoch's second big party get-together.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: With it, a message that echoes the well-known mantra of the early 1990s Tories, issued by former leader Michael Howard at party conference: "Prison works".
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: They are not just talking about adding on a few cells here and there, but spelling out a monumental increase in the numbers of people that the country locks up.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: That follows the announcement of a new "tough love" approach for young people trying to claim benefits.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Don't expect the shadow work and pensions secretary, Helen Whateley, to produce a moment as controversial as when the then-welfare secretary, Peter Lilley, proclaimed from the stage that he had "a little list" of benefit claimants he wanted to root out.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: But the Conservatives are determined to keep concentrating on the size of the welfare bill – believing it's right to do so for financial and moral reasons.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: You can expect to hear more in the week about fundamental conservative principles: people keeping more of their own money, government only stepping in when really required to, pointed concern about the level of the country's debt and public spending.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: And again, of course, that means Kemi Badenoch disavowing much of what the Conservatives did in office between 2010 and 2024, when the civil service grew, the tax burden grew, a law was passed to try to combat climate change, the list goes on.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: She'll set out at some length in the coming days what she sees as classic conservative first principles: the core beliefs the party was founded on and drifted from, she reckons, in the years gone by.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: If anything, Badenoch told interviewers this week the party was "finally saying what we believe" and "should be more aggressive" in displaying the party's core.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: The frontbench at last year's Conservative conference She believes the arrival of Andy Burnham makes that easier.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: There's a clearer contrast between the two.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: A senior ally of Badenoch says Burnham has "opened the door to it quite well, as he has harked back to the '70s in a way that I'm astonished by".
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Suggesting the pleasing atmospherics of Burnham's Labour are just that, atmospherics, the ally adds: "It's like a fairy story where he has come to the rescue of Britain and he has a wand in his hand and nothing else".
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: As we talked about a couple of weeks ago , the contrasts between Labour and the Conservatives are sharper now Burnham is in post, and the conference season is only serving to exaggerate that.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: They are both only too happy to emphasise it with their messages, retro or not, designed to show the true souls of their tribes.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: But while Badenoch might find it easier to argue clearly with Burnham, rather than tangle with Starmer over process, it is harder to face an opponent who, at least for now, is proving more appealing to the public.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: And while plenty of Conservatives are hopeful in private that Reform might have peaked, they can't be sure that's true, or that the swathes of voters who abandoned the Tories for Farage's party will return.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: Badenoch has always seemed allergic to the idea of doing any kind of deal with Reform, who she dismisses as a party of protest.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: And her allies hope, and some believe, that Reform's appeal will fade, making the Conservatives again the obvious alternative government.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: But fundamental arithmetic displays that, for as long as millions of voters on the right are tempted by Farage, it's harder for the Tories to triumph.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: One shadow minister admits "we've still got a whole battle on the right" even though "Kemi's boldness" is beginning to break through.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: So, in the coming next days, prepare for a "classic showing of Tory wares": an attempt by the party's leader to set out their fundamental beliefs about the country and how it should be governed.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: There are pockets of nerves that Kemi Badenoch risks rewinding to an previous era.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: One when another newly confident leader, David Cameron, ushered in the modern Tory party on the conference stage in front of digitally produced green foliage and sunlight.
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: One former cabinet minister warns that it's "the big risk – so easy to slip into an alienating divisive manner – nasty party stuff".
sentences.article_title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage

sentences.text: When it comes to policy, and striking the right tone, they warn that Badenoch must "be mindful that she has to win Cheltenham and Maidenhead as well as Clacton".

sentences.text: If buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the money to get there is a marathon.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: The "Your First Home" scheme , announced on Saturday, aims to help first-time buyers in England get on the housing ladder with a small deposit.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Currently a 5% deposit on the average UK house price of £272,000 plus moving costs and legal fees - will set you back about £16,850, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: That's daunting, but here are four ways that experts say you can at least make a start on saving for a deposit.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Depositing an amount you can afford into a regular savers account the day after you are paid is a good way to start, suggests Anna Bowes, savings expert at financial advisers The Private Office.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: "It becomes like another bill, but one that you can benefit from in the future," she says.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: The type of account that's suitable depends on your circumstances.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Some of the ones that pay the highest interest  are only accessible if you hold a current account with the provider, she says.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Other considerations are whether you can lock the money away for longer, to receive a better savings rate.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: If you don't have a buffer of other savings, then experts say an easy access account gives you the chance to dip into the money to pay an unexpected bill.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: You can save up to £4,000 a year in a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (LISA) and the government guarantees a 25% bonus.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: So, if you put the full amount in then the government will add £1,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: But there is a catch, that has left some people out of pocket .
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Money saved in a LISA can only be used to buy a first home up to the value of £450,000 - a threshold that has not changed since 2017.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: The only other time you can withdraw the money is after the age of 60 or in the exceptional case that you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Withdrawal under any other circumstances means you get hit with a penalty - so you could get back less than you put in.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Ministers are planning to replace the LISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, but there are no clear details yet about how it will work. 'I lost thousands in savings and my partner's money is in limbo' The earlier you start saving the more you can build up thanks to the magic of compound interest.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: In short, interest is added on a larger and larger pot as time goes by.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Bowes says that saving £50 a month from the age of 20 would give you about £41,000 in 30 years' time when you hit 50, assuming interest of 5% is paid a year.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Start 10 years later, and you'd need to save more than double - £101 a month - to have the same amount at the age of 50.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Investing in stocks and shares is another option , but the value of investments can go down as well as up.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Watch: What is compound interest?
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: An increasing number of lenders are offering mortgage deals with little or no deposit required.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: David Hollingworth, from L&C, points to mortgages that have deposits starting from £5,000 and allow people to borrow up to 98% or 99% of the property purchase price.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: They might not always be the best option , and not everyone will be eligible.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: And, of course, some first-time buyers turn to their parents for help.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Again that's not available to all , but a survey by the Nationwide Building Society suggests that more than half of parents who charge their adult children rent are putting some or all of the money towards helping their child save to buy their own home.
sentences.article_title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it

sentences.text: Audrina is asking for hospital food to be improved A 12-year-old girl who spent time in hospital battling an aggressive form of cancer has launched a petition calling for improvements to the food dished up to patients.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Audrina, from Derby, said despite receiving excellent care from doctors and nurses during her treatment, the food she was served often left her disappointed.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: She described the meals as tasteless and lacking in important nutrients she believes patients need while recovering.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Now she is urging the UK government to take action to raise standards.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: The Department for Health and Social Care said it welcomed ideas from campaigners like Audrina on how hospital food can be improved.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Audrina spent time in hospital being treated for cancer Audrina was diagnosed with neuroblastoma in 2018 but is now cancer-free after completing her treatment.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: However, despite being given the all-clear at the age of five, she has spent further time in hospital with another condition, cyclic vomiting syndrome.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: In this time, she says she feels hospital meals have not improved.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "The food is often lacking nutrition and it's important that patients have something to look forward to when they're going through a really tough time," she said.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "If you don't have the vitamins, minerals and proteins your body needs, it's going to slow your recovery down.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "I remember having a shepherd's pie and the mash was brown and burnt - and it was just served in the plastic pot it had been microwaved in." Audrina's mum says her daughter has always hated hospital food Her mother, Gemma, says Audrina has always hated hospital food and is determined to bring about change.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "We're just over 500 signatures but she's got to get to 100,000 [to be considered for Parliamentary debate] so there's a really long way to go yet," she said.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Audrina has also launched a new series on Instagram called £1 meals.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Gemma said: "She's going to be showing examples of meals which are healthy and tasty as well, so that hospitals can see they don't necessarily need to spend more money to get decent food." Audrina hopes the videos will help with her campaign.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "It's alright saying you can do this, but sometimes you need the proof.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: This will achieve that proof and that evidence," she said.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Audrina believes hospitals could make better use of locally-sourced produce and community support.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: She has also suggested growing fruit and vegetables at hospital sites as one possible way of providing fresher food.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Audrina's local MP Jonathan Davies is backing the campaign The petition has grabbed the attention of Jonathan Davies, Labour MP for Mid Derbyshire, who said he found out about it while knocking on his constituents' doors.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "I was really inspired by Audrina's energy and enthusiasm, informed by her personal experience of spending quite long period's of time in hospital," he said.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: "I said I'd get behind her campaign and make sure ministers heard what she had to say." Audrina has already visited the Houses of Parliament as part of her work and is hoping Davies can help her speak to the prime minster about the campaign.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "We want every hospital patient to receive food that is appetising and supports their recovery.
sentences.article_title: Girl, 12, campaigns for healthier hospital food

sentences.text: Verstappen took his first pole position of 2026 at Sepang Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Verstappen has dominated the weekend so far on Formula 1's return to the Sepang track for the first time since 2017.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Hamilton joins him on the front row to revive memories of their no-holds-barred title battle five years ago.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: But at nearly 0.3 seconds slower in qualifying, and with the pace Verstappen has shown all weekend, Hamilton's mindset on Saturday was to "just try my best to hold on to him tomorrow".
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: This was Verstappen's first pole position of the year - a remarkable statistic for someone who came within two points of winning a fifth world title last year after one of the all-time great fightbacks.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Red Bull started the year off the pace - the car was on average more than 0.5secs a lap slower than Mercedes in the first half of the year - and for a time there were questions as to whether Verstappen would stick around for 2027.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: But after being courted by McLaren, Verstappen signed a two-year contract extension over the summer break, saying he believed in the Red Bull project and didn't mind putting in the work to turn things around .
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Verstappen arrived in Malaysia after a run of three consecutive podium finishes, and with Red Bull hoping to prove out an upgrade that had seen them finish less than 0.2secs off victory in Baku last Sunday.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: In the tropical heat of Malaysia, around the demanding long corners of this track with perhaps the roughest surface of the season, the upgrade - centred on a new floor - has more than proved its worth.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "It's been an incredible result for us," Verstappen said.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "Looking at the season, how it started for us and the progression that we have made.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: At some tracks we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "We have been adding bits to the car and they have worked.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: When they work, you gain lap time, you have a better overall balance in the car.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "So with tyres that are very sensitive to balance, that gives you also more lap time.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "And then on a track probably where it's all very hot and you want a, let's say, stable balance or connected balance, then that's very important.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: And that's what we have found a little bit more over the last weekends." This video can not be played Team-mate Isack Hadjar, who missed the first three races after the summer break with a wrist broken while boxing as part of his training programme, says the car felt transformed when he returned in Baku last weekend.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "I jumped in a car that's way better than when I left it in Budapest," said the Frenchman, who qualified third, but will start eighth after a grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "Definitely, when you step out actually for three races and you come back, you actually notice a bigger difference.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: And the last two weekends have been surprising." A good car balance should put Verstappen in a good place for a race that will be dominated by tyre degradation in the stifling heat, whether the threatened rain holds off or not.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: This video can not be played Hamilton, for one, but also Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who under-performed slightly in qualifying because of a combination between an unusual tyre strategy and an error on an early run.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: The world championship leader's fourth place becomes third on the grid with Hadjar's penalty, and he can usually be relied upon to be a factor in the race.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Antonelli's main focus will be his advantage over team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points and starts four places behind, his momentum from his Baku win stalled, and somewhat perplexed as to his and his team's lack of pace.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: At Mercedes, the bigger question is over the aerodynamic upgrade they brought to the car this weekend.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Mercedes are lagging behind their rivals when it comes to developing their car this season, apparently at least in part because they front-loaded their spend early in the season.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: But this first big update since the Canadian Grand Prix in June has not yet proved the step they had expected.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: The question is whether that is to do with the parts themselves or the very specific conditions of this weekend, in the heat and on the rough track surface, which is putting the tyres through the mill, and massively limiting the useful laps teams can do in terms of set-up work.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Antonelli said: "With this new package, obviously the window of the way the car operates is different.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: So, we're trying to understand in which window the car performance is best, in the high-speed corner and low-speed corners.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "Our high-speed performance has been very strong this weekend.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: We were very quick in the high-speed, but in the low-speed we lacked.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: So, we need to understand why and try to move on and improve." As for the race, Antonelli said: "Track position is going to be very important.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Strategy is going to be really important.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "It's a race where we will attack.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: Because undercut (stopping first and gaining time on a rival on fresh tyres) is incredibly powerful.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "So whenever there's an opportunity, we should go for maybe an undercut and try to maximise our opportunity.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: "Tomorrow might be two stops, three stops.
sentences.article_title: 'Incredible' Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1 in Malaysia

sentences.text: But the only thing we know is that it's going to be roasting hot out there." Verstappen takes first 2026 pole ahead of Hamilton Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions How to follow Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the BBC

sentences.text: The famous Teufelsrad, or Devil's Wheel, from which videos are regularly posted online (file picture) The operator of a popular amusement ride at the Munich Oktoberfest has been handing out free cycling shorts to women, after thousands of voyeuristic videos emerged on social media.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Some videos showing women on the Teufelsrad , or Devil's Wheel, have been viewed millions of times.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: One is said to have made thousands of euros for a woman who posted it online.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: The Teufelsrad is one of the oldest attractions at the Oktoberfest, the annual beer festival which comes to an end this weekend after 16 days.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Its circular platform rotates faster and faster until its riders fall off, and the motion and speed often make skirts fly up.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Filming under skirts is illegal in Germany, and carries a two-year sentence in jail.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: However, critics believe the law does not go far enough, and the videos of women on the Teufelsrad in their traditional dirndl dresses often show their underwear.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Sometimes, the images have been digitally altered to show them naked, according to local broadcaster BR.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Elisabeth Polaczy says she has handed out more than 100 pairs of cycle shorts this year One woman made €9,000 (£7,650) from a single clip, according to BR, whose investigations found that a group of professional YouTubers from Ukraine and several people from Bavaria were behind the videos.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: At least 32,000 videos of women on the Teufelsrad have been in circulation, according to Munich-based daily Süddeutsche Zeitung.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: Some have apparently been viewed millions of times.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: The operator of the Teufelsrad, Elisabeth Polaczy, told the BBC that, for the past three years, she has been handing out free cycling shorts to women and girls wearing dresses, to protect them from people filming in the crowd.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: This Oktoberfest she has handed out more than 100 pairs, she says: "I want to do everything I can to make people feel secure." Polaczy, who is now 80, said donating cycling shorts wasn't cheap, but it was worth it for her own peace of mind.
sentences.article_title: Women given shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting

sentences.text: The hikes are part of immigration policy changes introduced to manage Japan's growing foreign population Japan has raised fees for foreigners seeking permanent residency in the country by 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955).
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim to manage its rapidly growing foreign population.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations".
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: "To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: Applicants who face financial hardship or are designated as refugees would be granted discounts.
sentences.article_title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times

sentences.text: An ancient bridge underneath Wimbleball Lake has resurfaced due to prolonged dry weather Months of dry weather and prolonged heat have revealed a bridge dating back to the Victorian times that had been submerged during the creation of a reservoir.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: The ancient stone Bessom Bridge flooded nearly 50 years ago when Wimbleball Reservoir was created at Exmoor National Park in Somerset.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: It was later replaced by a new bridge.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: In the summer, the Environment Agency declared that Wimbleball was one of the top three lowest reservoirs in the country after levels were recorded as "exceptionally low".
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: It is not known why some structures were demolished and others were not.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: The bridge dates back to the 1800s The former Bessom Bridge used to cross a stream that fed into the River Haddeo, while the new one crosses the north side of the lake.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: When water levels drop, the old bridge can be seen from the new one.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: Shipley said the changing landscape on Exmoor was "extraordinary".
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: "The photographs are incredible, they're just so dramatic of the bridge poking out from the silt and sediment that's covered it.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: Elsewhere around the county, traces of centuries-old gardens were found in Bishop's Palace in Wells , while relics of old structures were uncovered at Glastonbury Abbey due to the record-breaking summer temperatures .

sentences.text: Water levels at the reservoir remain low after prolonged heat and dry weather Wimbeball Reservoir, which supplies water to hundreds of thousands of homes across the South West, has a capacity of 21,320 megalitres - one megalitre is a million litres.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: The reservoir remains low following record-breaking temperatures over the summer, with a current capacity of only 21.1% as of 27 September, according to South West Water.
sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.article_title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed

sentences.text: Lee Heyes said he would love to know how the man he saved is getting on A man who risked his own life to rescue a stranger from drowning 30 years ago is trying to track him down.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: Lee Heyes jumped into a quarry when he was 15 after he realised the older teen had got into difficulty.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: The now 45-year-old, from Chorley, who has written a song about the ordeal, said instinct took over when the stranger, who he thinks was about 18 or 19, jumped in the water at Eccleston Delph and disappeared under the surface after getting tangled in reeds.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: "It has really bothered me ever since," he said.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: "I would love to know how he is getting on." Lee Heyes said writing a song about the ordeal has helped him Lee, who is a plasterer and singer songwriter, performing as "soundstruggles", recalls there being all sorts in the water - even cars at the bottom - when the incident happened in the mid 90s.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: He said it took him three attempts, diving deep under the surface, to find the teenager.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: After managing to untangle him, Lee said it was a struggle to get him back to the surface as he was "much bigger than me".
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: Lee got his friends to enter the water to help keep the teenager's head above the surface while he swam to get help from a dad who was in a dinghy with his son.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: By this point, Lee recalls being shattered but said the adrenaline spurred him on to raise the alarm.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: The dad then used the dinghy to get the teenager ashore.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: Lee said the stranger walked off afterwards without saying a word.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: "I presume he was in shock," he added.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: He said looking back it could have been a very different outcome.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: "I could easily have died myself that day," he said.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: Lee's message to anyone thinking of swimming in open water is "don't do it because it is so dangerous".
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: The trauma of that fateful day has never gone away and Lee believes it triggered anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: Lee, who is one of the stars at this weekend's Chorley Live which features 280 performances across 36 venues in the town and has more than 10,000 followers on TikTok, has written a song about the ordeal called Aqualung.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: The moving song has helped him deal with what happened, he said.
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: "It is a long time to carry that burden." He said the teenager had blond hair and was about 5ft 10in (1.78m).
sentences.article_title: Man desperate to find teen he saved 30 years ago

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: Chris Brain led the Nine O'Clock Service from 1984 to 1995 In the detailed written instructions given to the young women who worked without pay in the then-Reverend Chris Brain's house, there was a revealing demand.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The homebase team, as they were known, were to "do anything" the Church of England priest asked of them.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: Routine tasks - assigned on a rota 24 hours a day, seven days a week - included cooking, cleaning, ironing, shopping, looking after Brain's young daughter, and walking his dog.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: This housework was intended to free Brain for his mission of leading the Nine O'Clock Service (NOS), a radical congregation of hundreds of young people drawn weekly to a Sheffield church in the 1980s and 1990s by a fusion of rave culture, live music, environmental activism and liturgy.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: But the lengthy list of homebase team duties did not spell out other demands Brain made in the attic bedroom of his family's end-terrace house in the suburb of Crookes, heard jurors at his retrial on charges of rape and indecent assault.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: On Friday at Inner London Crown Court, the 69-year-old was found guilty of raping one woman in his congregation and four indecent assaults against three others .
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: He had already been convicted of 17 indecent assaults in August 2025 but faced a retrial as jurors could not reach verdicts on five further counts.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: Brain will be sentenced later this year and has been told he is facing a custodial term.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: His sentencing will conclude a dramatic and protracted downfall for a preacher who at one point had been preparing to take NOS global with expansion to the US.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The charismatic and domineering preacher, seen by many followers as a prophet, would routinely summon members of his congregation to "put him to bed" with sensual massages, jurors heard.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: Often Brain would strip to his underwear and expect kissing and sexual touching with the women, who feared being ostracised - or even damned - if they refused, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: "By displeasing Brain, you were displeasing God," explained one woman, who gave evidence last month during her former vicar's sexual assault trial.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: NOS outgrew St Thomas's, and in the early 1990s moved to Ponds Forge (pictured above in 1998) The movement took root in the early 1980s when Brain, his wife Lynne and small group of like-minded Christian friends joined St Thomas's church in Crookes.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: These dozen or so new worshippers - clustered around a band called Present Tense - were devout but disillusioned with traditional Anglican worship.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: Brain, their bassist and de facto leader, railed against "fancy golf club Christianity" which did not connect with them culturally.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: In 1984, the church's vicar Robert Warren gave the group an opportunity to run their own experimental service, every Sunday at 21:00.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The band - who had played gigs across the north of England and performed before U2 at the Christian festival Greenbelt - ditched their evangelical rock songs in favour of a new sound influenced by Sheffield's burgeoning electronic music scene.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: NOS was a sensation - attracting a youthful congregation of up to 600 people with an innovative blend of cutting-edge music, video, prayer, and dancing.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: "It's the most entertaining church I've been to.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: It's the best dance night in Sheffield," one worshipper told a 1990 BBC Radio 4 programme, which reported how NOS was "bridging the gap between the church and the people".
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The Archbishop of Canterbury told Brain he would be happy to see a NOS in every town and city in Britain.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The services, which later moved to a larger space at Ponds Forge leisure centre, were a huge production involving a crew of up to 150 volunteers - among them musicians, sound technicians, designers, security, and a trucking team.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: A new multimedia service was planned each week, with volunteers working unpaid throughout Sunday into the early hours of Monday morning to pull it off.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: Warren, who had oversight of NOS in its first years at St Thomas's, told the court he initially believed Brain's"controlling" nature helped to get things done.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: But as the popularity of NOS grew, the vicar noticed "cult-like elements" emerging.
sentences.article_title: How rapist priest exploited charisma to abuse his 'cult-like' congregation

sentences.text: The extension of the  bluetongue restriction zone should make it easier to move cattle without a special licence Restrictions aimed at controlling bluetongue, a virus that affects sheep, cattle and other livestock, are now in force across the whole of Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: The Scottish government said they should be seen as a "positive thing" which would make it easier for farmers to get uninfected animals to market without requiring an individual licence.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: The disease, which can be spread by insects such as midges, does not affect people and poses no risk to food safety.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Bluetongue was first detected on farms in south-west Scotland in August and there have now been more than 100 infected animals in 41 locations, including four outside the original restriction zone .
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: While no danger to humans, Bluetongue can cause fever, swelling, lameness, birth defects and difficulty eating for cows and particularly sheep.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: In some cases, animals die or become so ill they have to be euthanised. 'I feel guilty': The farmer whose lamb had Scotland's first case of bluetongue What is the potentially deadly bluetongue virus?
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Scientists believe the disease probably spread to Scotland after infected midges were blown across the border from England but the risk of transmission is now  falling as the midge season draws to a close.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Agriculture Minister Jim Fairlie said extending the restriction zone was a "sensible step" at the current time that would make trading easier for the livestock industry.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: It means the whole of Scotland, along with England and Wales, is now covered by a restriction zone, removing the movement barriers between high and low-risk areas because they all now have the same disease status.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: "We don't want people to be restricted given the fact that it's now at this time where the vets think there's unlikely to be transmission of the disease," Fairlie added.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Farmers are being urged to have early conversations about vaccinations for next year Farmers must still notify the authorities immediately when an animal displays symptoms.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Infected animals are generally required to remain on-farm for a minimum of 60 days, but the majority of healthy, non-infected animals can be traded.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: Fairlie said vaccination remained the most effective way for farmers to protect their animals from the worst effects of bluetongue.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: "People need to be thinking about the vaccine programme for next year," he said.
sentences.article_title: Bluetongue restriction zone extension a 'positive thing' for farmers

sentences.text: "There is no other way to protect their stock properly so they should be speaking to their vet and looking forward, thinking about what the vaccination programme looks like for them." Some farmers reported difficulty getting hold of the vaccine this year as demand rose suddenly as cases were reported in England.

sentences.text: It plans to close manufacturing sites at North Lakes near Penrith, Cumbria, Pettigrews in Kelso, Scotland, Seaham in County Durham and Enfield, Greater London, though distribution operations would continue to run from the latter.
sentences.article_title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs

sentences.text: The proposals will also impact manufacturing operations at its Treforest site in Wales, but this will also continue as a distribution centre for the business.
sentences.article_title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs

sentences.text: The chain, which has headquarters in Newcastle, said its retail shops would not be affected by the proposed changes and like-for-like sales had grown across its managed stores.

sentences.text: It said the plans would save it about £20m across the 2028 and 2029 financial years.
sentences.article_title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs

sentences.text: The changes would take place over the next two and a half years, with parts of Greggs' manufacturing processes relocating, the firm said.
sentences.article_title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs

sentences.text: The range of products manufactured at its Clydesmill Glasgow and Manchester locations would be reduced and production of tinned bread at Gosforth would be stopped.

sentences.text: The Governor of the Bank of England has said regulating artificial intelligence (AI)  "is not the right place to start" but instead called first for "rigorous" testing to find vulnerabilities and create safeguards to contain risk.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Writing his first-ever article for Substack, Andrew Bailey said the risks around AI were "real and increasingly significant".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: He said AI development should not be halted or prohibited - "on the contrary, the benefits are immense" - but added there must be a system for intervention and to establish boundaries in which AI operates.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The debate about the potential risks surrounding the rapid development of AI and what it means for humanity has intensified in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The bosses of leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI have called for development of the technology to slow down and for an internationally co-ordinated approach assessing risks and putting safeguards in place.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: OpenAI recently announced that it would not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns .
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns Under the agreement, the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: In the UK, Bailey said "important work" was underway in testing AI - the UK has set up the AI Security Institute - which, he said, should help form part of a set of standards.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But the pace of progress must accelerate," the bank governor said, though he added: "We should proceed with a degree of humility." He said, with testing, there will be failures and "models will behave unexpectedly".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: But, he said: "That is not evidence that testing has failed, rather it is evidence of why testing is necessary." Bailey said that testing should not be seen as an alternative to future regulation - over time a more formal regulatory framework might emerge.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But regulation is not, in my view, the right place to start." Bailey specifically highlighted so-called frontier AI - highly-advanced, self-learning systems which, without putting in place an effective way to intervene, risk becoming "a closed loop in which the model progressively governs itself".

sentences.text: Trump met top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday to discuss AI US President Donald Trump hosted a meeting of top technology bosses on Tuesday for what he called "an extraordinary gathering" of the minds that are "building America's Golden Age".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The guest list included leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta and Google - all key figures in the US AI industry.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The meeting came as some tech executives and experts have called for tighter oversight of AI, citing concerns about the potential risks it poses to humanity.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Here are three key takeaways from Trump's tech summit at the White House.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump took questions from the media for around 30 minutes alongside top tech leaders after the closed-door meeting.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The president said the executives had signed a "morally binding" document that would serve as a "form of protection" from AI's potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Under the agreement, which Trump posted online , external , the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The firms also agreed to implement safeguards to keep models operating as intended and quickly detect and fix any issues.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "It's almost like a constitution, in a way," Trump said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "And the biggest people in the world signed that, and I signed it as president." Trump with top tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday Trump added that he will set up a board to oversee the safety of AI tools.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: He did not specify who would be on that board.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Zuckerberg said the accord gives the "American people and customers the confidence that the technology works" as intended, calling the meeting a "historic conversation".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Amodei called it a way "to win safely", referring to the president's comment earlier this month that "whoever wins AI, wins".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: But not all technology experts are impressed with the accord.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Nanyang Technological University AI governance researcher Jose Miguelito Enriquez said the pact shows "emerging consensus" but does not address whether AI developers should be held accountable for incidents.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: It is "deeply unimpressive" and comes despite calls from some world leaders and industry figures for tighter regulations around the technology, said law professor Kimberlee Weatherall from the University of Sydney.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The agreement appears to allow firms to "define what counts as safety" and does not state what consequences there are for any breaches, Weatherall said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "The accord should be ignored, for the distraction it is," she added.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Why Trump is all-in on AI despite the warnings Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI's risks in response to calls from some industry figures for tighter oversight of the technology.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: On Monday, OpenAI said it had scrapped the release of its latest flagship AI model , GPT-6.1 Astra, over safety concerns.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The company's security controls have come under intense scrutiny after high-profile incidents involving its technology, including its models accessing Australian government platforms without authorisation .
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Jeannie Paterson from the Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Ethics at the University of Melbourne said self-regulation could mean that companies set "only minimal safeguards".
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The agreement inspires "very little confidence" as recent incidents of AI going rogue suggest companies have been undisciplined in their approach, she added.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Trump also reiterated his support for the rapid expansion of data centres - the crucial computing infrastructure that powers AI.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The rollout of data centres has drawn pushback around the US over concerns about electricity usage and their potential impact on communities.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Data centre construction has also emerged as a potential political obstacle for Trump's Republican party ahead of the US midterm elections in November.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: A survey conducted by Marist Poll in partnership with NPR and PBS News , external earlier this month found that 65% of registered voters opposed data centres being built in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Responding to those concerns, Trump said tech companies would work to make people "happy" about the construction of data centres.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "These big, powerful, very rich, very smart companies are going to be making massive contributions to communities," Trump told reporters.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Also on Tuesday, Trump signed an executive order instructing US government departments and agencies to start using the terms "SI" and "Super Intelligence" and should no longer acknowledge the use of the term artificial intelligence.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: SI will take the place of AI in "official correspondence", websites, reports and other forms of communication, the order said.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "As these capabilities continue to improve, they increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence," the order said.

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: But some experts said after Trump's UN speech that they thought the term was unlikely to gain widespread traction because it is a name typically used to refer to more advanced systems.

sentences.text: Huel is best known for its shakes, which it says are a nutritionally complete meal An advert for Huel meal replacement shakes has been banned by the advertising watchdog for encouraging or condoning "irresponsible" dietary practices.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ad featured Huel brand ambassador Spencer Matthews sharing an anecdote of a person he met who "only eats Huel" and who won a 260km race "by miles".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said that viewers could assume from the ad that replacing all conventional food with Huel was "nutritionally appropriate" and was compatible with elite physical performance.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Huel said Matthews' anecdote was not "a recommendation or instruction" and the purpose of the ad was to challenge the misconception that Huel could replace every meal".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The video, which appeared as a sponsored Instagram post and YouTube pre-roll ad, featured Matthews speaking to Huel founder Julian Hearn in the style of a podcast.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The Instagram post included the caption: "Here's how our founder uses Huel.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Spoiler alert it's not for every meal." In the video Hearn said that he has Huel products for breakfast and lunch during the working week, but has a "traditional meal" when he goes home.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: In response, Matthews said that when he was competing in an ultramarathon, he met a man who "only eats Huel".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Matthews said he was initially sceptical that the man would be able to manage the race, but then said: "He won it by miles, like literally just left us all in the dirt." Hearn replied: "In an ideal world, you should have nutritionally complete whole food.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "Most people either don't do that or can't have the time to do that, and therefore that's where Huel fits in the gap." In the advert Spencer Matthews talks about an athlete who "only eats Huel" Huel, which is based in Hertfordshire, was founded by Hearn in 2015.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: It is currently in the process of being bought by French conglomerate Danone .
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The market for so-called complete nutrition products, aimed at time-poor, health-conscious consumers, is thought to be worth $5.9bn (£4.4bn).
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA received four complaints about the advert, which challenged whether the content was irresponsible.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: Two of the complainants also challenged whether the health claims in the ad breached the ASA's advertising code.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA acknowledged in its ruling that the ad "did not explicitly recommend that consumers replace all conventional foods with Huel", but consumers could nonetheless interpret the anecdote as "an acceptable dietary practice".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: "By presenting exclusive consumption of Huel in that context, the ads suggested that the complete replacement of conventional food with Huel was nutritionally appropriate and presented no barrier to achieving a high level of physical performance," the ruling said.
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The ASA also upheld the complaint regarding the health claims as it ruled Matthews' anecdote about the ultramarathon athlete "implied a beneficial relationship between consuming Huel and the ability to sustain exceptionally high levels of physical and endurance performance".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: In its response to the complaints, Huel said the advert "unambiguously positioned Huel as part of a balanced diet for occasions when preparing whole food was not practicable".
sentences.article_title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals

sentences.text: The company pointed to Matthews reacting with "extreme scepticism and disbelief" to the idea of a person solely consuming Huel.
