sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This video can not be played Polanski calls for 'national fair rent guarantee' Zack Polanski has urged voters to back the Greens to force changes from Andy Burnham, arguing his party has the power to move Labour in "the right direction".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: In his speech to the party's annual conference, the Green leader said that "sustained pressure" from his party had made forced Labour into changing its stance on issues including climate and its stance towards Israel.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: He told activists in Brighton that Labour had failed to take action on housing, as he called for a three-year cap to limit rent rises in the private sector.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: And he said that voting for the Greens would force changes from the government, telling members: "Vote Green, and watch Labour move".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Polanski arrived in Brighton facing questions over his leadership of the party amid signs the Greens' rise in popularity last year may have waned, and how he would respond to Labour's change of leadership under Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: In his half-hour address, he did not mention the Conservatives or Reform UK but launched repeated attacks on Labour's record in office.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: He criticised Labour for making "slogans without action" on the cost of living and vowed only his party would end "Rip Off Britain".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: And he was particularly critical of Labour's record on housing, where he accused the party of failing to take on the "powerful vested interests of developers and big landlords".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Instead, he urged the government to enact an "emergency brake" on private rents, under which they would be prevented from rising above the lowest of consumer price index measure of inflation, wage growth or 2%, for three years.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: He argued that pressure from the Greens in the face of government "inaction" had forced Burnham into calling an emergency Cobr meeting this summer amid record-breaking hot and dry temperatures.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: The Greens, he added would not "hesitate" to tax "extreme wealth", as he repeated the party's call for a so-called windfall tax on back profits - an issue where the government has faced pressure from unions.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: "Through our sustained pressure – and our historic wins – we have held the worst instincts of the Labour government in check.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: "And we have started to move them in the right direction.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: But we can't wait for them to get there on their own." He also sought to draw a clear dividing line with the government on the issue of oil and gas, ahead of looming decisions for the government on whether to approve the Rosebank oil field and Jackdaw gas field.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Burnham has stuck to Labour's manifesto commitment not to issue new oil and gas licences, but has left open the possibility of approving the two sites.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: This summer's wildfires, Polanski told the conference hall, should prove the "final nail in the coffin for new oil and gas".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: He began his address by celebrating his party's surge in membership since his election as party leader a year ago, and electoral successes including the hundreds of councillors it gained in May's local elections in England .
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: But his speech did not touch on an issue that could divide the membership over the weekend, ahead of a probable vote on a motion put forward by members that describes Zionism as a form of racism.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: The motion defines Zionism as an ideology in support of "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and seeks to shift the party's position to supporting a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: The current form of the motion has drawn criticism from senior figures, including deputy leader Rachel Millward, who earlier described it as "problematic".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Green MP Sian Berry would not confirm how she planned to vote on the motion but said she could "absolutely see and feel how strongly many members feel we should be saying even more".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Under Green Party rules if the motion passes it would officially become party policy, but would not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Polanski has said he wants to see the motion amended to specify that it should not be used to discipline Jewish members attending synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: He is also supporting a change that would replace the call for a single Palestinian state with backing for a "lasting settlement granting equal rights for all" to be "shaped and determined by Palestinians themselves".
sentences.article_title: Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

sentences.text: Asked by the BBC if he believed that Zionism is racism, Polanski said it would depend on how the term was defined.

sentences.text: Badenoch had been the party's leader and the leader of the opposition for almost a year.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: It is an anecdote which underlines the scale of the challenge Badenoch faced at that conference, an event her allies are now with distance willing to acknowledge was make or break for her leadership.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: And it is an anecdote which also underlines that, far from break her, that conference represented the start of a major turnaround for Badenoch.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: Twelve months on, Badenoch will arrive in Birmingham this weekend in total command of a party whose leading lights are beginning to permit themselves the occasional flicker of optimism after years of misery preparing for, and then experiencing, a brutal election defeat.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: Yet for all that Conservatives now believe their leader is an electoral asset, they still face an existential threat from Reform UK and the challenge of how to adjust their strategy to face a new prime minister, Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: The answer to both those issues for Badenoch is a focus on the economy.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: "Stronger economy, stronger country" will be the party's conference slogan, with the two speeches Badenoch gives - one on Sunday, the other on Wednesday - building on announcements she has made in the past two weeks about cutting benefits for the long-term unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: Welfare spending is increasingly seen by the Conservatives as a core battleground with Labour.
sentences.article_title: Tories aim to be election-ready ahead of party conference

sentences.text: During Labour conference they derided the event as the "Welfare Party Conference".

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has set out his plan to transform Britain, including by ending the existing state pension triple lock from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In his first Labour Party conference speech as prime minister, Burnham also said he wants to pave the way for greater public control over housing, water and energy services, and potentially reform the UK's electoral system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: After days of questions over how to fund his social care reforms in England, Burnham pointed to changing the triple lock to generate "significant savings".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: His plans would see the state pension increase every year at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power In front of a packed hall and watched on by family and friends, Burnham spoke for more than an hour - at times pausing and appearing to hold back tears as he referred to his father, Roy, who died earlier this month .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Arriving on stage to the sound of "All Together Now" by Liverpool band The Farm, Burnham made the song title a theme of his speech.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said he wanted to "draw a line on a decade of division" and to "stop doomscrolling on posts running Britain down".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham also told conference that he wants to "put the country on a new path" and recalled his family's "working-class aspiration" and how the government wanted to "unlock" this for others.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: There was an expectation that Burnham's time in Liverpool for his party's conference would see him flesh out his vision for the future of the country.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In the conference hall, he offered more details albeit with some of the proposals relating to the content of the Labour manifesto at the next general election rather than delivering immediate action.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham's plan to offer free at the point of use social care in England is among those being developed so it can be put before voters in 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said it would be "fully funded and not through borrowing".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Explaining his long-held ambition to make changes, he raised his family's experiences - including how his grandmother Kitty's engagement ring was "ripped from her finger and stolen in a care home".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He argued a national care service was a "landmark" policy that would be "as significant as the creation of the NHS itself and utterly essential to securing its future".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Before turning to the pension triple lock changes, Burnham accepted he may "pay a political price" by trying to make the reforms but argued "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The triple lock was introduced in 2010 by the coalition government and designed to ensure the value of the state pension was not overtaken by the increase in the cost of living or the incomes of working people.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: It means the state pension rates rise every April by either inflation, earnings growth or 2.5% - whichever is the highest.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham said this will stay in place until 2030, at which point he would like to "adjust it".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said: "The state pension will continue to rise every year at least by prices or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: And it will hold its value relative to earnings over time so that pensioners will always share in the rising prosperity of the nation.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "But this change will generate significant savings which we will use to build up our national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "Some may not realise it but older people with nothing more than the state pension, or only a little more, can find themselves paying care charges today from that small income.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Under my plan, this will no longer happen." Officials have suggested the change could save £15bn a year by 2040.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Jonathan Cribb, deputy director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said savings "are likely to be relatively small in the first few years, but rise substantially over time".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He also said "we should not expect this reform to save enough that it could fund universal social care in the next parliament".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union, told the BBC she believed the government should have "pulled another lever", such as a wealth tax, rather than making changes to the triple lock.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The political backlash was immediate.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said "more tax rises are inevitable" under Labour's plan, while Reform UK's Nigel Farage accused the PM of "launching an offensive against our elderly".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said families "cannot wait until after another election and it can't be funded from the pockets of our poorest pensioners".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Andy Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel greet delegates in the audience after he delivered his keynote speech Elsewhere in his speech, Burnham said he wanted to repeal "Margaret Thatcher's ideological ban on public ownership of water companies".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The PM said legislation will be put before Parliament, adding the changes will "start a 10-year journey to a very different water system", which includes new powers for mayors to hold "companies to account".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham said it will be made easier for councils to acquire private rented homes in poor condition if landlords refuse to take action after being issued warnings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said the government will change the law "if necessary".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham also told delegates that "Brexit has done more harm than good" before he indicated he wanted to explore closer UK-EU ties.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Ahead of talks expected later this year with EU chiefs, Burnham said he would set out the "different options" for Britain's "long-term relationship" with the bloc.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Good luck to the commission.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: I shall be interested in what it comes out with." Burnham also said he wants to "invest" in young people and change the education system and welfare system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said: "We will rebuild a system of comprehensive education in this country, with parity between academic and technical." Burnham added there needs to be a "fundamental rethink" of the welfare system to fund new opportunities for young people.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the PM's conference speech contained little more than "half measures, reannouncements and tinkering".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: What are your views on the triple lock?

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has promised that Labour will fight the next general election on a pledge to change the UK's voting system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: In his first party conference speech as prime minister, he announced plans for a national commission to explore options for electoral reform.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He invited other parties to work with the commission to ensure "everyone's vote counts, and everyone's voice is heard".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He has previously supported moves towards a proportional representation (PR) model, telling last year's conference that "PR's time has come".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Westminster's first-past-the-post system, under which candidates with the most votes in each seat are elected, has been called into question as the UK political landscape has fragmented in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Debate over the system has intensified since Labour amassed a huge parliamentary majority with a 34% vote share in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Around 100 Labour MPs recently supported a parliamentary amendment in favour of setting up a commission to examine alternative options, a move Burnham himself supported last year when mayor of Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Any move to change the voting system would be supported by the Liberal Democrats, who had previously urged Burnham to introduce proportional representation before the next election, which must be held by 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: However, any move away from first-past-the-post is likely to be resisted by the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Reform UK backed introducing PR at the last election, but there has been speculation that its enthusiasm for the move may have since cooled.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Speaking to broadcasters after Burnham's speech, Reform leader Nigel Farage said he was open to debating a potential change to the system "at some point" but other issues were "far more urgent".
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: He added: "Is this an absolute priority for the general election after the next one?
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: I don't believe that it is." Support for changing the voting system is also not universal within Labour, with deputy leader Lucy Powell acknowledging that "parts of the Labour Party" are not in favour of it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Speaking to Politics Live on BBC 2, she said she personally backed electoral reform but declined to specify a proposed new system, adding there were "lots of models" available.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: At the last UK election the Liberal Democrats backed the introduction of a single transferable vote (STV) system, which is used for Scottish council elections.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Other options include the additional member system, a hybrid model that combines first-past-the-post with regional party lists that is used to elect members of the Scottish Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Welsh Senedd was elected for the first time using a closed-list proportional representation system .
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: The Green Party supports electoral reform but Green MP Ellie Chowns said: "The PM cannot acknowledge the unfairness of a system capable of handing power to a government with a minority of the vote share, and then say the answer is to let that happen exactly once more before he fixes it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham to fight next election on pledge to change voting system

sentences.text: "Burnham must act with urgency to immediately jumpstart the National Commission, guarantee timely progress, and ensure its recommendations are delivered in time for a fairer voting system to be in place at the next general election." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?

sentences.text: Angela Rayner took aim at the 'injustice' of leasehold in her conference speech Leaseholders will be given extra protections from "cowboy" property agents and hidden fees, Angela Rayner has announced.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The housing secretary told Labour's annual conference the government would legislate for a new independent regulator and launch a consultation to cap "rip off" administrative fees.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The changes would cover the estimated five million leaseholders in England and Wales who can be forced to pay a landlord for simple changes to their home, despite having bought it.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner told party activists she had heard of leaseholders being charged £250 for permission to own a pet and £400 to change their front door.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said people in these situations were "powerless against the vested interests that only take, while giving nothing back in return".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government is already legislating , external to ban new leasehold flats, described in Labour's 2024 election manifesto as a "feudal" system where people own the right to occupy a property via a lease for a limited number of years from a freeholder, or landlord, who owns the land.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Through the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill , ministers want a commonhold system where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Now, Rayner is taking aim at the web of management companies that operate between leaseholders and their effective landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said the sector had many decent businesses which were "undermined by far too many cowboys, crooks and con artists".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: People excited at buying their own homes are "tricked" into using in-house services, meaning that "with no transparency or accountability, vultures can take advantage", Rayner added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: "We will legislate for an independent regulation to rein these cowboys in," she said, announcing legislation for an independent watchdog of property agents.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This includes estate agents, managing agents and estate managers.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This regulator would be able to set codes of practice, such as standards of conduct and proper complaint handling for those they regulate, and property agents will be required to obtain a licence.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: If they fall foul of the required standards, the regulator would have the power to take their licenses away, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to bring forward the changes "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said new legislation would create the power for caps on permission and administration fees leaseholders pay to landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: These caps would cover freehold estates and privately managed estates where people can face additional fees for making cosmetic changes to their properties and requesting documents like building safety certificates.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: A public consultation will be launched to help decide the rate of caps.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: It comes in addition to an already-announced £250 cap on yearly ground rents paid by leaseholders in England and Wales, which had stalled during the change of prime minister over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government has said it expects the limit on ground rents - an annual fee paid by leaseholders to their freeholder - to come into force in late 2028, but MPs have called for this to be brought forward to late 2027.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner said she was "capping and then scrapping" ground rents, indicating she may try to go further than a cap.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: In her speech, Rayner did not mention the government's housing target of building 1.5m homes in England by the next election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She admitted earlier this month there was only a "slim chance" of hitting it .
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Last week, ministers announced a new Your First Home policy to help first-time homebuyers in England with a deposit of 2.5%, similar to the Help To Buy scheme introduced under the Conservatives in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said she plans to strengthen council powers to take over empty homes to meet the need for council houses and tackle homelessness.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: But this was criticised by the Tories as a "desperate" attempt by Labour to try to hit its housing target.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Union boss Sharon Graham has been an outspoken critic of Labour governments in the past Unite the Union general secretary Sharon Graham has warned the prime minister that scrapping the pensions triple lock would be "morally wrong", as Andy Burnham prepares to deliver his first speech to Labour conference as PM.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: Burnham told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that he wants to use his speech to set out his "vision" to introduce an NHS-style social care system, free at the point of use.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: There is growing speculation about how such a care system could be funded, including removing the pensions triple lock in the future.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell told BBC Breakfast the party is committed to the triple lock, which was in the party's 2024 manifesto.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: The triple lock, which has been in place for 16 years, means state pensions rise every April by at least 2.5% or in line with the highest of prices or earnings.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Graham said axing the triple lock risked repeating the unpopular removal of the Winter Fuel Allowance under previous prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: "Instead of going to try and pick the pocket of pensioners, we need to move over to the other side of the equation and think about things like wealth taxes way before we try to stop something like the triple lock," she said.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: "Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it [social care], to take away their security, is wrong - I think its morally wrong," she added, highlighting how current pensions are the lowest of the G7 countries.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: On Tuesday morning, Powell said the lock was a manifesto commitment, and asked whether it would stay in place until the next election, she said: "I can absolutely assure your viewers watching this that we are committed to the triple lock, it's in our manifesto.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: He said social care in England is "as unfair as American healthcare, where the most vulnerable in society can lose everything, they can be wiped out" and indicated "nothing is off the table at this moment in time" on funding.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than £23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: Alan Milburn, the former Labour minister who is currently leading an independent review into young people and work for the government, has said scrapping the triple lock to fund social care is "the sort of call" the prime minister is "prepared to make".
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: In the BBC's Political Thinking podcast, Milburn was asked if Burnham's new social care plans could be funded by getting rid of the triple lock, he responded that Burnham was "exactly the sort of person who can take the big decisions".
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: He said: "Andy is absolutely right about this - the social care system is broken...
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: That is going to be a really big call.
sentences.article_title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss

sentences.text: "But it's the sort of call that I've got no doubt - from everything, and every conversation I've been in with him - it's the sort of call that he is prepared to make." Burnham is also expected to announce a new government body to invest in Britain's electricity grid, branded Great British Grid , in his speech.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham's comments on Manchester City's rule breaches sparked controversy The rows circulating around Manchester City are huge, and they are only going to get bigger.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: The Premier League has concluded that City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: This, clearly, matters for the club, but that is just the start of it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: It matters for Manchester, it matters for the Premier League and so, crucially, it matters for the UK's image around the world – because England's top flight is a colossal global brand.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: In other words, this matters whether you like football or not.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: Added to all of this, Andy Burnham pitches himself as Mr Manchester and is a big football fan.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: The man who was the mayor of Greater Manchester a matter of months ago is now the prime minister, and so finds himself caught up in it all at a local level, a national level and a diplomatic level.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: Diplomatic, because rows will rage over the extent to which City's ownership is separate from the Abu Dhabi state.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: And the state is a big UK ally.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: All of this is why I thought it was in the public interest to put a series of questions to Burnham about it when I spoke to him on Wednesday as the Labour Party conference concluded in Liverpool.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: His comments, in his interview with me , followed by no fewer than two attempts to backtrack 24 hours later, amount to perhaps his biggest self inflicted tangle since he arrived in Downing Street in July.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: He will have expected to be asked about Manchester City, but he didn't expect sustained scrutiny about it.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: One particular exchange prompted a lot of interest.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: I asked if he was worried that Manchester City's owners from the United Arab Emirates might sell up.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: It is worth quoting his answer in full.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: "Well, I would be really concerned to lose them.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: "I can't intervene more in the process.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: It would be wrong for me to do that.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why Andy Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters

sentences.text: Burnham is putting the proposals at the heart of a new goal to bring UK energy costs in line with other nations in Europe within 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: He promised on Tuesday to have an "honest conversation" with the public and take on the "difficult issues" that have been ignored for too long.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: "A publicly-owned company that will challenge the private sector operators," he told the Labour conference.

sentences.text: "It will increase competition, drive down costs and speed up connections.
sentences.article_title: Burnham says public body will invest in electricity grid

sentences.text: "So businesses can expand and grow more quickly." There are a number of reasons for the high energy prices in the UK , part of which comes from state subsidies given to private companies to modernise the grid.

sentences.text: In his Labour conference speech, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would "adjust" the triple lock on the state pension to help pay for a new "national care service" in England from 2030.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: While his proposed reform is likely to reduce public spending on pensions, analysts say it would be unlikely to save enough money between 2030 and 2040 to pay for comprehensive social care reform.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at the key figures.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Since it was introduced by the coalition government in 2011, the triple lock has guaranteed that the UK state pension rises each year in line with whichever is the highest of inflation, average wages, or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Burnham said that from April 2030, instead, it would only rise in line with the highest of inflation or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The prime minister added that "it will hold its value relative to earnings over time".
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: That is important because in some years the triple lock has meant the state pension has risen faster than earnings.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: "The removal of this permanent ratchet is to be welcomed and marks a substantial step towards a more sustainable and predictable state pension system," the IFS says.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: It estimates that the present triple lock will increase annual state pension expenditure by £16bn a year by 2026–27, compared with if it had risen in line with average earnings growth since 2011.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: It says that if the new lock had been in place instead, spending would be £9bn a year lower than it currently is.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: There is considerable uncertainty about future savings though because the cost of the triple lock is linked to the future volatility of people's earnings and inflation, which are impossible to confidently forecast.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Moreover, analysts think it could take more than a decade for the reform to deliver major savings.

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) - the government's official forecaster - analysed how much , external shifting to just an earnings-linked state pension in 2030 would cost relative to keeping the triple lock.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: This is similar to what Burnham is proposing.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The OBR did not identify any significant savings for the government from such a shift until 2034.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: By 2040, the annual saving was estimated by the OBR to be 0.2% of GDP, equivalent to £6bn a year in today's money.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Downing Street has said the prime minister's planned change will save £15bn a year by the end of the 2030s , external , equivalent to £11bn a year in today's money, but it did not provide detail on how it reached this figure.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The IFS estimates that the reform will save around £4bn a year, in today's money, by 2035.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: But it cautions that future savings are "very uncertain" and says the change "could easily save nothing at all if earnings growth is strong".
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Different social care reforms come with different price tags.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The Health Foundation think tank has estimated that imposing a lifetime cap on an individual's care costs of around £86,000 in England, as proposed by the official report for the coalition government by Andrew Dilnot in 2011, would cost the government around £4bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The think tank estimates that introducing a Scotland-style system of "free personal care" - which does not include accommodation, food and everyday living costs - would amount to around £7.5bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: And the cost of creating a universal and comprehensive social care system , external in England would be around £18.5bn a year extra by 2036.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The government has not set out the full details of how the "national care system" will work, but has clarified that while an individual's direct care costs would be covered, their accommodation costs in a residential or nursing home would not be.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Nevertheless, if it implemented a universal and comprehensive social care system then the expected revenues from the proposed reform could fall short.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Jonathan Cribb of the IFS said the pension reform "will not be the answer to funding universal social care".
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: This could put pressure on a future government to raise revenues from other sources - either from tax rises or spending cuts elsewhere - to pay for a comprehensive social care service in England.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was fatally attacked by Rolando Torres-Pena, 22, at a mental health trust in east London A mental health trust in east London, where a man was killed by a fellow patient , has been warned further deaths may occur unless staff issues are addressed.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was strangled by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena at Newham Mental Health Centre, which provides care for acutely mentally ill men, in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The coroner has sent a report to the Trust and NHS England raising serious concerns about the care the two men received.

sentences.text: It follows a six-day inquest in September during which the senior coroner for east London, Graeme Irvine, concluded that neglect had more than trivially contributed to Flint Cahan's death.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: On the night of Flint Cahan's death, staff on the ward were found to have been asleep on the job and on their phones for long periods.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) says the failings identified were "wholly unacceptable" and that it has undertaken a "significant programme of work" to improve inpatient services.

sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: The document also says there were delays in starting CPR on Flint Cahan when he was discovered, that staff misled the police as to what the patients had been doing on the night of the incident, and that staff colluded with each other to take two-hour unauthorised breaks.

sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: "The findings in this inquest are strikingly similar to the findings of an inquest before this court in 2021, remedial measures reported in that case do not appear to have been implemented effectively by the trust", the report says.

sentences.text: "Findings of dishonesty on this scale are extraordinarily rare in a coronial investigation.

sentences.text: The public are entitled to expect a clear explanation of how this was allowed to happen and what is being done to ensure it never happens again," says James Cahan, the family solicitor and Hugo's cousin.

sentences.text: The coroner also criticised NHS England for not making independently produced reports into patient safety at Trusts publically available.
sentences.article_title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed

sentences.text: An NHS spokesperson said "patient safety incident investigations should always be published, with any necessary redactions to protect patients' identities, while making sure the lessons and learning are clear".

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has delivered his first speech to the Labour conference as party leader and prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: It was no surprise to see Andy Burnham tieless and roaming the conference stage in Liverpool, unanchored by the traditional leader's speech podium.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: But despite the relaxed TED talk vibe, this was sober and serious speech.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: He set out major new policies - not always a given on these occasions - and spoke with real emotion about his family and working class roots.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: There were few jokes - and in stark contrast to his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer's speech last year, he did not mention Nigel Farage or Kemi Badenoch once.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: But he also avoided mention of some of the trickier issues he faces, such as welfare reform and how his government will pay for promised increases in defence spending.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: It went down extremely well in the hall.

sentences.text: We counted 11 standing ovations in just over an hour.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: In the end, it was a bit more nuanced than that.

sentences.text: He said he would "honour" Labour's commitment to keep the triple lock until the end of the current Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: But from April 2030, the state pension would rise every year by inflation or 2.5%, whichever is higher, under Burnham's plans - and it will be increased in some years if needed to keep pace with average worker earnings.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: The change, he said, would "generate significant savings" to fund his long-held ambition of creating a National Care Service in England.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: "But someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off." Burnham has made no secret of his desire to scrap Westminster's first-past-the-post voting system.

sentences.text: And his announcement of a national commission on electoral reform went down very well with many in the hall, who have been calling for it.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: "We will contest the next election with a manifesto commitment to change the electoral system so that everyone's vote counts and everyone's voice is heard," he said to cheers.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: As he neared the end of his speech, Burnham appeared overcome by emotion and it looked for a brief moment as though he could not carry on.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: He was speaking about his father Roy, who he lost to Alzheimer's earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: Five takeaways from Andy Burnham's Labour conference speech

sentences.text: "If only, if only he had been able to appreciate that moment of the family in Downing Street," Burnham said of his first day in his new role.

sentences.text: "The son of a man who failed his 11-plus becoming prime minister." The longest ovation of all came when he pledged to "use this job to build the kind of Britain my dad wanted to see – and fight with everything I've got to keep it together".
