sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Charlotte McCann said the trial gave her hope for the future Charlotte McCann has been dealing with severe pain from endometriosis since she was 14.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It became so intolerable as an adult she had to leave her chosen career.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She would wake up in the night vomiting, and on some days Charlotte found she could not stand or get out of bed.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It is a myth that endometriosis is a painful period condition - rather, it is a system-wide inflammatory disease where cells, similar to those which line the womb, start to grow in other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: This can be on the bowel or in the lungs - and the cells multiply, creating raw and angry sores.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Those affected can wait years for diagnosis, and there is no cure - meaning women are left grappling with debilitating pain that can affect their relationships, work, education and mental health.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Now aged 27, Charlotte hopes a new pain management programme for the condition, which is being trialled as part of a £2.3m study, might help others in her position.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: The UK-wide study, led by the University of Aberdeen and NHS Grampian, will include pain medication alongside other treatments such as physiotherapy, and will investigate whether a personalised plan can improve quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: This video can not be played Hope for new endometriosis trial in Aberdeen Charlotte, from Huntly in Aberdeenshire, is currently living with stage 4 endometriosis , external .
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She had to abandon her career in corporate finance due to the pain, and now works as a freelance pet-sitter when she can.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "I would wake up in the night vomiting and I was always worried that maybe my appendix had burst or I had a kidney infection or something like that," she recalled.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "The pain would come on so strong, I wouldn't be able to even sit up straight, I wouldn't be able to stand up.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "It was heavily disrupting my life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: I couldn't focus on anything, and I couldn't sleep or eat because of the pain.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "There's no way I could continue my nine-to-five job when I could barely sit up." Charlotte said she had years of not knowing what was wrong, until an MRI scan confirmed endometriosis.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Women can wait years for an endometriosis diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: New tech could change that Emma Barnett: We can't ignore this disease that leaves one in 10 women like me in agony It affected her bladder, and has spread to other parts of her body.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "I am now on very strong opioid painkillers to try to get on top of the pain, but they make me feel very sick, to the point I can't eat, so I have lost a lot of weight now as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Charlotte described being in so much pain that there are days when she cannot get out of bed.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She also has to use walking aids to get around due to the pain in her back brought on by her endometriosis symptoms.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She tried surgery to remove the tissue in question, but the symptoms returned.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Asked about the new trial, Charlotte said she was optimistic.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Once participants are recruited, they will take part in a 12-week personalised programme - called an endometriosis-specific pain management programme (e-PMP).
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: The project will evaluate whether this strategy can offer more effective treatment for women who find their pain is not adequately controlled by surgery or medication.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It includes cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-informed psychotherapy, specialist physiotherapy, guidance on relationships, intimacy and communication, and medication to reduce side effects.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds Pre-menopausal women will either receive the new programme alongside existing standard care, or existing standard care alone, with the results of each approach then compared.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Eligible participants will be recruited to the study by their specialist.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Consultant gynaecologist Dr Lucky Saraswat, an honorary senior lecturer at the university, and lead for Aberdeen Endometriosis Centre at NHS Grampian, is heading the study.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Dr Lucky Saraswat is leading the new study "Endometriosis is one of the most common yet under researched causes of chronic pain," she said.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "Many women continue to suffer even after surgery or medication.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "This study will help us understand whether a tailored, interdisciplinary pain management programme can offer meaningful, long term improvements in quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "If effective, e-PMP could become a vital new treatment option, particularly for women who wish to avoid repeated surgery or hormonal therapies, or who are planning a pregnancy." Alongside the clinical results, the study will also aim to assess cost effectiveness.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Prof Anthony Gordon, director of NIHR's health technology assessment programme, said many women could face years of "agonising" symptoms with few long-term options.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "High-quality research is essential to break this cycle and deliver treatment that addresses the full, complex impact of endometriosis," he said.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Rosie Stewart passed away in 2003 aged 33 They gathered to remember "a girl like no other" - a trailblazing rugby player whose exploits on the pitch were cruelly cut short by her death at just 33.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: Last Saturday, on a sunny September afternoon two teams from two different corners of Northern Ireland came to City of Derry to contest the Rosie Stewart Memorial Bowl.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: Stewart, from Londonderry, won four caps for Ireland between 1999 and 2000 and was a founding member of Ulster Women's Rugby but, in 2003, she died after being diagnosed with breast cancer.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: The memorial match is held every year in her memory and also to promote female health, a cause her sister Colette Risely said would have been close to Stewart's heart.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: Kelly Gormley plays for the City of Derry women's rugby club "I think the more we do the talking, the more lives we will save," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: But what was going on off the pitch was just as important, with a women's health discussion held before the match hosted by the Western Trust's Jacinta McCool and fitness coach Claire O'Hagan.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: O'Hagan's spoke on female strength and conditioning and the impact of the menstrual cycle on athletic performance, while McCool focused on breast and cervical cancer awareness.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: It was a "poignant" event for City of Derry player Kelly Gormley, who said a number of squad members have been affected by or had breast cancer.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: Jacinta McCool works at a midwife for the Western Trust "It's at the forefront of our minds," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: "I think when you are delivering information and awareness, it's information you're taking to 20 or 30 girls." Jacinta McCool, whose message of early detection of breast or cervical cancer leads to better cure rates, said it was important to raise that awareness.
sentences.article_title: The Irish international rugby 'trailblazer' and her legacy of cancer awareness

sentences.text: "Hopefully anybody that hears one thing, they go off and tell three or four of their friends, then we are reaching a much bigger audience." For Gormley, Stewart was a "pioneering" player in her efforts to grow the women's game.

sentences.text: Lisa Carroll was only 41 was she was diagnosed with the rare form of ovarian cancer A mum-of-three who was diagnosed with a rare cancer has urged other women not to dismiss their symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: When Lisa Carroll, 47, from Coventry, returned from a family holiday in August 2021, she thought she was suffering from irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), a kidney infection or something minor.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Instead, she was told it was mucinous ovarian cancer (MOC), one of the rarest forms of ovarian cancer in the UK.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I thought I had possibly a bit of IBS or a kidney problem or something like that.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I was in quite a lot of pain," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Next year, Carroll and her husband are looking forward to celebrating their 20th wedding anniversary After calling NHS 111, Carroll was sent to hospital in Coventry where medics discovered a 12cm cyst on her right ovary.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: She was told it did not appear particularly sinister and was placed on a waiting list for surgery.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Within a month, a cyst the size of a fist had grown to the point that I could feel it like a football in my stomach.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Pain and discomfort got worse and I felt shattered emotionally and physically", she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: By December, scans revealed the tumour had grown to 20cm and was beginning to rupture, so three days later she underwent an emergency procedure to remove the tumour, a fallopian tube, her appendix and surrounding tissue.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Two weeks later, doctors gave her the diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Following surgeries and chemotherapy, Carroll is approaching her five-year anniversary of being cancer free The cancer is exceptionally rare, with only around 200 cases diagnosed annually in the UK, said Ovacome, an ovarian cancer charity.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Some ovarian cancers are really sneaky, hang around for years and you've got no sign of any symptoms at all", said Carroll, who works as the CEO of Lifespace Trust, a Warwickshire-based charity for young people.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "The fact that mine grew so quickly was what alerted them as early as they did." Yet despite losing her hair and enduring months of treatment, she says the biggest challenge was something she had not been prepared for.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I got chucked into early menopause and that was the bit I massively struggled with.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I didn't know what was depression and what was menopause." The Ovacome charity is hosting a fundraising walk in Cannon Hill Park, Birmingham on Saturday "I didn't know what was a cancer symptom and what was a menopause symptom.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't open the washing machine, the dishwasher or the oven.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't cook anything on the hob because I'd just have this awful hot flush.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I was incredibly emotional." Today, Carroll is cancer-free and approaching the five-year milestone that will see her formally discharged from oncology care.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I do not underestimate how fortunate I am that my long-term outlook is a lot brighter than for many," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "That brings with it a kind of survivor's guilt." She has since became involved with Ovacome, which connected her with others facing the same fears.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "They became my safe space," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "They helped me to connect with other people who understood what I was going through.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: They made an incredibly scary and isolating time feel far more manageable." Now preparing to take part in the charity's annual fundraising walk, Carroll hopes sharing her story will encourage others to trust their instincts and seek help when something feels wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: The fundraising walk takes place at Cannon Hill Park in Birmingham on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.

sentences.text: Communities in several parts of Nepal are mourning loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Speaking from a damp, blue tent in Battar, a town north-west of Kathmandu, Buti Tamang told BBC Nepali: "We used to live in a hut, but now there is nothing.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: We have lost so many of our relatives." "Now it is raining and the tent leaks, so we've been facing a difficult situation.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: We have nowhere to go," said Ramesh Ghale, who also had to flee his home.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Many Nepalis have been made homeless and are staying in emergency tents, as a new wave of extreme weather strikes Several trekkers and their guides say their journeys back down the mountains have been treacherous, taking up to three or four days and requiring them to pass collapsed roads and swept-away bridges.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Jake Stacy, a 21-year-old from Suffolk, found himself stranded with his guide in Yak Kharka, upper Manang, due to heavy snowfall last week and decided not to continue to the Thorang La pass, the highest point of the circuit.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: "We made our own paths on mountain slopes," he said, after returning to base camp in Pokhara on Tuesday night.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: "It was quite steep and we were clambering because there was river below… It was very muddy and very wet.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: "Many trekkers were helicoptered out," he added.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Jake Stacy and his guide had to craft their own paths on the mountains to return after heavy snowfall Australian Andrew Graham and his guide Prem KC said they had to cross more than 15 landslides after they decided to return from Manang village.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: "A few of them were quite dangerous, the residual risks have grown now." The two got stuck when they reached the village of Chame, which had been evacuated due to the risk of landslides, and had to spend a night in the jungle, Graham said.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: A massive landslide has partially blocked a river which passes through Chame, causing a temporary lake that has inundated houses and a key bridge.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Authorities have been trying to release the water for the past three days using excavators but have not been very successful, locals told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Meanwhile, trekking guide Tse Ring Doma said she and her group had to cross 28 landslides.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: She added that authorities had been clearing many of the landslides "surprisingly fast".
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: But four bodies have been recovered and 12 people remain missing after an avalanche near the base of Himlung Peak , close to the border with Tibet.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: A representative of the local trekking authority, the Annapurna Conservation Area Project, said some 700 trekkers were still waiting in Pokhara to embark on the Annapurna Circuit.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: "We have been holding back all these people who want to go to the Annapurna Circuit trek, although we are under pressure from the trekking industry to announce the route open," he said.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Indian visitors who often visit the ancient temple Muktinath on a Hindu pilgrimage had been asked to fly from Jomson to Pokhara instead of drive down, due to a cut-off road, he added.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: Most of the old trekking trails on the Annapurna Circuit have been unused in recent years after the introduction of roads, except for small pockets of Manang and Mustang districts.
sentences.article_title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal

sentences.text: But now operators say many trekkers have been using these abandoned paths to return, as the main roads have been washed away in some sections of the circuit.

sentences.text: Michael Sheen investigated Wales' toxic legacy in a BBC iPlayer documentary Member of the Senedd from all parties have urged Welsh ministers to work with the UK government to make sure polluters pay for cleaning up contaminated land.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: A motion introduced by Plaid Cymru MS Niamh Salkeld, backed across party lines, also calls for a UK fund to investigate and remediate sites where costs cannot be recovered, and for a framework to test affected land.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: The calls come after a BBC documentary by Michael Sheen examined claims toxic waste poisoned people at 14 sites in Wales and England.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: A Welsh government minister promised a plan to "progressively restore post-industrial land" and protect communities from "potential risks".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Sheen went to Westminster to urge MPs to support a testing programme.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: Salkeld, who represents the constituency of Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, said her motion was about "making sure that the legacy of our industrial past is managed properly and fairly".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "It's about having a clearer national picture of contaminated land," she said.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "It's about prioritising the sites where the risks are greatest.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "It's about giving local authorities the support that they need, and it's about making sure that where possible, those responsible for pollution contribute to the cost of putting it right.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: Reform MS Andrew Griffin said communities across Wales living near sites that are potentially unsafe "deserve answers".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "They deserve a system capable of establishing the facts, and where action is needed, they deserve to know that the money and the determination are there to see it through.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: He said this demonstrated "that all levels of government need to act fast and need to act together in partnership" to tackle this pollution.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "Councils, citizens and communities cannot afford the cost of remediation, nor can they afford to wait any longer for action." He called on Plaid Cymru ministers to "stand up for the people of Wales by taking urgent action where it can now".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: Niamh Salkeld said a "clearer national picture of contaminated land" is needed Conservative Janet Finch-Saunders said local communities "should be able to understand where these sites are located, what risks have been identified, what action is being taken, and whether that action is satisfactory".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "Regular inspections and up-to-date public registers would help," she said.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "We must ensure that lessons are learned from previous incidents where contamination occurs, the response should be timely, coordinated, and proportionate, with clear responsibility for investigating the source.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "This is not simply about dealing with contamination after it has occurred.
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: He said he had heard the "calls for action", pledging he would "ensure that former industrial land is made safe".
sentences.article_title: Michael Sheen campaign on toxic waste sites wins Senedd backing

sentences.text: "I will protect public health and deliver long-overdue environmental justice for the communities that have been most affected by this," he added.

sentences.text: Bob Epsom (l) and a Lost Woods volunteer recording ancient trees for the mapping process A project which aims to restore ancient woodlands in Sussex has hit a significant "milestone" with over 5,500 trees now recorded.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: Since March 2024, volunteers with the Lost Woods project have been recording ancient, veteran and notable trees across a 121-sq-miles (314-sq-km) area from Lewes to Storrington.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: According to the latest figures, they have now recorded 5,570 trees, a number which Lost Woods outreach adviser, Bob Epsom, said is more than "we expected" and signifies a "milestone" for the project.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: "When we look at the map of it, we can see the new clusters of trees being added...that's where the volunteers have been active," he said.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: The Lost Woods is a partnership with four charities: Woodland Trust, Action in Rural Sussex, Sussex Wildlife Trust and Small Woods Association.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: The work, funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund, is part of a wider Lost Woods restoration programme which Epsom said comprises "19 individual projects".
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: About 20 volunteers are each given a square kilometre area to cover, and once recorded and verified, trees are added to the Ancient Tree Inventory which has been mapping the oldest and most important trees in the UK for 20 years.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: The volunteers are working to find and record every ancient and veteran tree in the project area by next year, and Epsom, who leads the team, said they still "have a reasonable amount to cover".
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: The biggest proportion of trees, 2,743, are veteran, survivors which have developed some of the features found on ancient trees.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: The remainder fall into a different category of tree.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: According to Epsom, these trees are "very important for the landscape, (and) very important for biodiversity" because of their fungi.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: Epsom said the mapping process was "only the first step", and that ultimately, there was a wider goal.
sentences.article_title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected

sentences.text: He said: "We need to make sure that trees are recognised, cared for and protected so that they can continue to support wildlife and communities for generations to come." sentences.text: The event included a field trip to Lihou Island exploring its ecology and archaeology Environmental experts, conservation groups and businesses from across the British Isles and France have gathered in Guernsey for the 26th Inter-Island Environment Meeting.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: The annual event, co-ordinated by the Guernsey Nature Commission, brings together delegates to share ideas and develop joint projects aimed at protecting the natural environment.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: This year's theme, Nature for the Next Generation, includes talks on subjects ranging from seabird restoration and woodland resilience to butterfly monitoring in Sark and citizen science projects.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: A Sixth Form Environment Meeting gave young people the chance to present environmental issues that matter to them and contribute ideas for the future.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: Students will take part in workshops linked to Guernsey's upcoming Marine Spatial Plan, helping shape discussions about the future protection and management of the island's seas.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: Angela Salmon, head of education at the Nature Commission and a member of the meeting group said inviting sixth formers to share the environmental issues that mattered to them "makes perfect sense".
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: Among those attending was Sebastian Dufour, an independent consultant for the Alderney Wildlife Trust, who joined a field trip to Lihou Island exploring its ecology and archaeology.
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: He said he had learned about a Benedictine Priory site "which is very interesting" and discovered there had been "a really remarkably large industry in harvesting seaweed".
sentences.article_title: Island hosts inter-island environment summit

sentences.text: Dufour said he particularly valued the collaborative nature of the event, adding: "We're all coming from different islands and we're all facing similar challenges." He said the annual meeting provided an opportunity to "learn from each other" and "share our successes and failures and everything".

sentences.text: David Knott, director of horticulture, said Edinburgh's Palm Houses are iconic After six years and an unprecedented botanical operation, Edinburgh's famous Palm Houses are back.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: The historic glasshouses at the Royal Botanic Garden have been closed to the public  for vital restoration work.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Hundreds of plants had to be temporarily moved while repairs were done on the 19th century buildings - the vast majority of them surviving the experience.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: But members of the public are once again able to enjoy the redesigned space.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Sadie Barber is delighted the palm houses are now being used in the way they were intended The shutdown had to happen because the buildings had become leaky and rusty and needed a complete overhaul.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Glass house curator Sadie Barber is delighted that, after years of disruption, the palm houses are once again being used for their intended purpose - to protect rare and and endangered plants, and to allow people to enjoy the space.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: The plants were decanted to temporary homes, and then carefully moved back into the renovated space.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Sadie says this has been a great achievement that wasn't without risk.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "I think whenever you move a plant and you take it out of the ground and then you stick it in a pot, it's going to suffer or it's going to get under stress.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "So there was a bit of trepidation when we picked up the biggest plants, moved them to another place, and left them there for a number of years.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: It feels like a huge achievement getting all these plants back in here and having them actually so well placed.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "The glasshouse team have done an enormous job, a really exceptional job of getting the plants looking like they belong.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "So it's great to see them actually thriving already." Thousands of panes of glass have been replaced during the restoration The buildings have undergone a huge amount of work.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: More than five thousand panes of glass have been replaced, and the once corroding ironwork has been repaired and repainted.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Stone work has been renovated and a partition wall between the two houses has been knocked down to create a light and airy space which shows off the historic architecture and living plants.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Prof Julia Knights is the Regius Keeper of the Botanic Garden.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: She says they have a wide range of plants and species, many of which are endangered.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "We've got palms, conifers, ferns, begonias, all of those families, plants are hugely important in our living collection and many of them are extinct in the wild," she said.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "So what the palm houses are doing is helping to protect so many of these species, and many of them of course have medicinal properties for human health.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: It had grown too tall for the glass house and had to be cut down and couldn't be stored.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: But some seedlings were kept, and so its legacy has not been forgotten.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: One of the Sabal palm's descendants is growing in its place.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: David Knott, the director of horticulture at the Botanic Garden, said: "Hopefully, because we've planted it in this glass house which is a bit taller than where it was previously, hopefully it will last a bit longer than the previous one did." He is happy to see the new one growing in place of the old giant tree.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "There was no way that we were actually going to ever be able to transplant the Sabal palm.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: And that was probably one of the hardest, most poignant parts of the whole process." The Sabal palm tree is thriving under the same roof as its parent, although it is significantly smaller David Knott hopes the people of Scotland will welcome the return of the glass houses.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "For many people in Edinburgh and throughout Scotland and throughout the world,  the palm houses in Edinburgh really are one of the most iconic features of the Botanic Garden here.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: And we hope when we reopen, we will be able to welcome people and they'll be able to enjoy the space as it was always intended to be." Sadie Barber says there are signs that the plants are enjoying their new home.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "You can see new growth coming out of some of those plants that are now in the ground.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: One thing people will notice is little new croziers coming in, coming up from the fern crowns.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: "When you see that unfurling you know a plant is happy.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: And if you look around there's just so much life.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: It's been an enormous job, but a really well done job.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: So we are overjoyed" The restoration keeps the palm houses looking much as they were intended, but using modern techniques and materials which should guarantee the future of these much-loved buildings.
sentences.article_title: Six years, hundreds of plants and one tree casualty - Edinburgh's Palm House returns

sentences.text: Steve Backshall, from Bagshot, wants as many youngsters as possible to be exposed to the natural world Wildlife presenter Steve Backshall has told how he sets out to make nature "adventurous" and "cool"  for children rather than preach to them.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: The presenter, known for programmes including Deadly 60, wants as many youngsters as possible to be exposed to the natural world.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: He spent his own childhood in a house in Surrey filled with rescue animals and said it helped inspire the passion for wildlife that later shaped his career.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: Speaking in London ahead of his Deadly Live show in Brighton , external on 29 October, he said what made his work exciting and worthwhile was seeing that there are "thousands and thousands of kids out there who have a passion for natural history".
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: He said his parents took on a smallholding in their 30s, adding: "We filled it with rescue animals, about which we had no idea, we were making everything up as we went along." Backshall recalled it as a "crazy version" of the TV sitcom The Good Life.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: He said: "That was my childhood and it was absolutely incredible." Backshall studied at Canterbury Christ Church, carrying out research into venoms from amphibians, and later received an honorary doctorate from the university.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: Explaining his focus on the world's most formidable predators in his TV series Deadly 60, he said: "We deliberately deal with animals like birds of prey and sharks and crocodiles and snakes and spiders and scorpions, big cats, that kind that everyone is fascinated by.
sentences.article_title: Backshall makes nature 'cool' to inspire children

sentences.text: The Nasa-led team of scientists took samples of ancient rock from the north-west Highlands Nasa scientists are studying rocks in the Scottish Highlands to help them understand if there was once life on Mars.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: The US space agency announced last year that its Perseverance rover had found potential biosignatures , markings on rocks possibly made by ancient microbes.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: This summer, scientists took samples from a geological feature called the Stoer Formation , external around Clachtoll, in Assynt, in the north-west Highlands.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa said the area's rocks formed in environments comparable to ancient Martian lakes and rivers, but could also hold evidence of microbial life from 1.2 billion years ago.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Scientists surveying rocks at Clachtoll in Assynt earlier this year Perseverance, shown in a concept image, has detected potential biosignatures Clachtoll is a small crofting community on the Sutherland coast about 100 miles north of Inverness, and is a popular destination along the North Coast 500 tourist route.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa's Goddard Instrument Field Team, which specialises in studying Earth's extreme environments, led the research expedition.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Experts from the universities of Glasgow and Cambridge were among those involved.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: They took rock samples from cliffs for further analysis.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Nasa said: "Though Mars is dry today, the Martian landscape, like our own planet's, is shaped by an ancient history of flowing water.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: "Both worlds have layered areas of mudstones and siltstones rich in clay minerals.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Last year, technology which will be used in the search for evidence of Martian life was tested by a University of St Andrews team at Lower Diabaig, in Torridon.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: The rocks in the area are billions of years old and similar to those found on the Red Planet.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Eight years ago, a Nasa Mars rover, Curiosity, explored a part of the planet named after Torridon .
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Martian geological areas and features have been named by Nasa after places on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Nasa heads to Scottish Highlands in its search for life on Mars

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, who has died at the age of 86, will perhaps be best remembered for presenting the BBC series That's Life!
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: While the programme ran for two decades, one episode in particular stands out for many.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: She presented the hugely popular BBC One show from 1973 to 1994, drawing in huge audiences.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: One of Dame Esther's most memorable career moments came during an episode in 1988 - the footage of which has gone viral several times over in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Dame Esther had been told the story of Nicholas Winton, the man who had organised the rescue of 669 children from Czechoslovakia, which was occupied in 1939 by Nazi forces.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Sir Nicholas Winton in 2014 receiving the highest order of the Czech Republic, the White Lion.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Sir Nicholas was able to rescue the mainly Jewish cohort of children after briefly visiting Prague.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: He was knighted in 2003 for his humanitarian work.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Sir Nicholas, who was born to German-Jewish parents, made a list of the children that needed sponsorship and found homes for them to go to in Britain.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: He worked alongside activists and humanitarians , external in Czechoslovakia to navigate complex political obstacles, such as getting children to Britain through the Netherlands, which had closed its borders to Jewish refugees.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Sir Nicholas was ultimately successful due to a House of Commons ruling on allowing young refugees in the country, which had been passed a couple of months before his rescue mission began.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: With the help of his mother, he put photos of the children in British magazines such as Picture Post to help find them homes and organised for hostels to take in some refugees too.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: He managed to raise money to cover travel for the children and provide them with essentials when they reached British soil.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: His incredible work went largely unreported for nearly 50 years - until his wife found a scrapbook in their loft, which contained names of children he had rescued.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: It was given to Holocaust researchers, who helped track down some of the children he had helped.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Sir Nicholas' story became national news when he appeared on That's Life! in February 1988 and Dame Esther Rantzen told viewers about his story.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen on the set of That's Life! in 1978 Speaking in February 2024, Dame Esther said when she first got in touch with Sir Nicholas, who she called Nicky, she "congratulated him on his extraordinary achievement".
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: She told The Radio Times , external he had expressed some disappointment about his efforts, commenting that "not enough" people had been saved.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: "I was devastated that he felt he had failed.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: I wanted to prove to this extraordinary man that every life he had saved was precious," Dame Esther added.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: She invited him onto That's Life and during his first appearance, his scrapbook was shared with the audience, and two women he had saved as children - Vera Gissing and Lady Milena Grenfell-Baines - revealed their identities to him on TV.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: They were sitting either side of Sir Nicholas, who had no idea of the surprise - something Dame Esther recalled as "incredibly moving".
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Lady Milena is one of the most well-recognised Holocaust survivors in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: She left Prague with her younger sister Eva at the age of nine, travelling on a special train arranged by Winton.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: The two sisters were looked after by a Tameside family until their mother arrived the following year, having escaped via Norway.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.article_title: Watch: Moment Esther Rantzen reunites man with children he saved from Nazi occupation

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, who has died at the age of 86, was best known for presenting the BBC TV programme That's Life!
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Over two decades, what started as a consumer programme with quirky asides became renowned for its high-profile campaigns, notably against child abuse.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It resulted in Dame Esther setting up Childline, a national telephone helpline for children suffering abuse or neglect.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying
