sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, broadcaster, campaigner and charity founder, dies aged 86 How That's Life! gave Esther Rantzen a career-defining moment Esther Louise Rantzen was born in Berkhamsted, Hertfordshire on 22 June 1940.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Her paternal ancestors were Polish Jews.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Her father, Henry, who worked as a broadcast engineer for the BBC, had moved the family out of London to escape German bombing during World War Two.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The family returned to London when the war ended.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She later recalled she hated the grey streets of the capital after the semi-rural idyll in which she had spent her early childhood.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: After a spell at a private school, run by what she recalled was a sadistic headmistress, she went to the North London Collegiate School in Edgware, and then to Somerville College, Oxford, where she read English.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen [centre] had an idyllic early childhood She became an enthusiastic member of the Oxford University Dramatic Society and of the Experimental Theatre Group.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen then secured a job as a trainee studio manager with BBC Radio, before moving to television as a researcher on the satirical show BBC3, which had been created by Ned Sherrin.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She met documentary maker Desmond Wilcox when she approached him in a BBC bar and asked him to give a talk to a local youth club.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: He asked her to dinner and offered her a job on Man Alive, the BBC's current affairs programme.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The pair later began a relationship.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The relationship caused huge tensions in her department, not least because Wilcox's wife Patsy, one of Rantzen's best friends, also worked at the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: By 1968, she was working on Braden's Week, a consumer programme fronted by Canadian presenter Bernard Braden.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: A decision to allow the researchers a short spot on air gave Rantzen her first on-screen TV experience, where she made a favourable impression on the producers.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: In 1972, Braden was sacked by the BBC after he appeared in a commercial for Stork margarine and his show was dropped.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: A year later, the programme was resurrected, given a new title, That's Life! and Rantzen was selected as the main presenter.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Dame Esther made her first TV appearance on Braden's Week Braden was sanguine about Rantzen's promotion but his wife, TV presenter Barbara Kelly, was publicly contemptuous of the decision and accused Wilcox of being instrumental in her appointment.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Launched in May 1973, That's Life! became an almost instant hit.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Recorded just before transmission on Saturday nights, it was initially a consumer protection programme investigating viewers' complaints about shoddy service and faulty goods.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Over the years it grew to include more quirky items.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It initiated the Jobsworth award for over-zealous bureaucrats and council officials, and Heap of the Week, in which failing domestic appliances would be destroyed on screen in a variety of ingenious ways.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Over the years, Rantzen was joined by a series of co-hosts, including Paul Heiney, Chris Searle and Bob Wellings, while the comedian Cyril Fletcher read his Odd Odes.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The show quickly became something of an institution but her relationship with Wilcox was causing problems behind the scenes.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Patsy Wilcox had reluctantly agreed to a divorce after Rantzen became pregnant, and Rantzen and Wilcox went on to marry in 1977.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: But there were accusations from some BBC staff that Wilcox, who was her boss as well as her husband, was furthering her career, pointing out that BBC rules forbade married couples working together.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Wilcox resigned in 1980 and set up his own successful production company.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: That's Life! ran for 21 years Rantzen also found time to devise a new talent series, The Big Time, which launched the career of singer Sheena Easton.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She became involved with the team behind the new ITV breakfast programme, TV-am, but dropped out before it went to air in 1983 so that she could remain at the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: By the 1980s, That's Life! had expanded its remit away from basic consumer issues to take on the role of campaigner.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The appearance of Ben Hardwick, a child desperately in need of a liver transplant, launched a drive to raise the awareness of the need for organ donors.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: As a result, Ben received a new liver at the age of two, but died a year later.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Other campaigns helped introduce the replacement of hard surfaces in children's playgrounds with softer material and a change in the law to enforce the wearing of children's seat belts in the rear of cars.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Not everyone was happy with the new format and there were complaints that a serious, and sometimes emotionally draining sequence, was followed by a quirky item on, for example, rude-looking vegetables.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The programme continued to maintain its high viewing figures after a move to Sunday nights, but the television landscape was changing.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The BBC's show Watchdog and ITV's The Cook Report were bringing a much harder edge to consumer journalism.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The death of Desmond Wilcox prompted Rantzen to launch a campaign to support older, lonely people The final That's Life! was broadcast on 19 June 1994 and featured a look back at both the highlights of the programme and Rantzen's own campaigning.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Possibly the most important and lasting result of any That's Life! campaign was the setting up of Childline in 1986.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It followed a number of incidents, featured on the programme, including one in which a toddler had starved to death, locked in a bedroom.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen persuaded the BBC after the programme was transmitted that a helpline should be set up so that children suffering abuse or neglect could call in confidence.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: In the 48 hours it was open, it was inundated with calls.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: This led to Rantzen campaigning for a 24/7 service to be set up.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Childcare professionals claimed it would be impossible but she managed both to raise the money and persuade BT to provide premises and a free phone line.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: By the time Childline merged with the NSPCC in 2006, it had 12 centres in the UK and the idea was quickly copied in many countries abroad.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen also devised and presented Hearts of Gold, a programme that celebrated previously unknown people who had been responsible for good deeds.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: When That's Life! came off air, Rantzen continued to present her own afternoon talk show, entitled Esther, on BBC Two.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It ran for 600 episodes and received two Bafta nominations.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Desmond Wilcox died in 2000 leaving Rantzen bereft.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She wrote a series of articles about the problem of loneliness among older people, which she described as "a creeping enemy which erodes confidence." She eventually set up The Silver Line, a 24/7 phone support system which offered advice, information and support to those who felt alone and unwanted.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Dame Esther set up Childline after a feature on That's Life! about a toddler who had starved to death, locked in a bedroom Rantzen also went on to make an appearance on the ITV show I'm a Celebrity, Get Me Out of Here in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She wrote a number of regular columns for newspapers and magazines and also involved herself with more than 50 charities.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Following the MPs' expenses scandal in 2009, Rantzen announced she would stand for parliament in Luton South.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She pitched herself against the sitting Labour MP, Margaret Moran, who had claimed expenses in excess of £23,000 for her second home in Southampton.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Moran stood down two days later but Rantzen fought the seat in the 2010 General Election, coming fourth with just over 4% of the vote.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Rantzen was made an OBE in 1991 and CBE in 2006.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: In the 2015 New Year Honours list, she was appointed a Dame Commander in recognition of the two helpline services she set up.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: The following year she warned of the social media pressure on children in the digital world, urging families to "be aware" of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Speaking on Desert Island Discs in 2019, Dame Esther told presenter Lauren Laverne that her own broadcasting career would not be as successful if she had joined the industry now as a young woman, because she would not be "pretty enough".
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Esther Rantzen poses after she was made a Dame at an investiture ceremony at Buckingham Palace in 2015 In an interview with The Mirror in June 2023, she spoke about her diagnosis with stage-four lung cancer.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: It "made me realise how very lucky I've been in my life," she said, "working with Childline and the Silver Line, and meeting so many fascinating and inspiring people".
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "I'm not good at regrets.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: What I treasure most are the fantastic friendships I have made thanks to That's Life! during the last 50 years, the people I met, and the team who worked so hard, and laughed so hard, together for so long." Six months later, she told The Times she did not expect to live much longer.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "Last January," she explained,  "I assumed that I would probably not be around for my birthday in June, and that I'd definitely miss this Christmas.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "But when I met my oncologist I realised how ignorant I was and what gargantuan strides medicine has made recently.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "Has my diagnosis taught me any lessons valuable enough to pass on?
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: A year later, she witnessed the House of Commons vote in favour of the first stage of a Bill that might make a medically-assisted death legal in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: A similar bill was introduced to the Scottish Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Although Dame Esther knew that she would not live long enough to take advantage of any new law, she said she wanted to protect other families from "the same agonising experience".
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "In the olden days, doctors would ease you out of life and the difference was it wasn't necessarily with your consent," she said.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: In March 2025, her daughter confirmed that the drug that had kept Dame Esther alive since her cancer diagnosis was no longer working.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: They had always known that its effects would be temporary.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: She added that she was now too frail to travel to Switzerland to end her life.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "I need to be needed," she said.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "It's what makes you get up in the morning, and makes you feel when you go to bed that the day has been well spent.
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: "There's a real pleasure in feeling somebody needs your help and that you actually have made a difference."
sentences.article_title: Dame Esther Rantzen: That's Life! presenter, Childline founder and campaigner for assisted dying

sentences.text: Kgomotso Mathekga says a lack of male role models is fuelling violence against women in his neighbourhood "I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Especially when they are both drunk." "I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her." Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We broke up and I no longer see my child.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am." At a nearby tavern, a group of men have pulled their chairs into a circle in the dust.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: At the centre stands Itumeleng Stephen Tamaga, known locally as Bra Steve.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group clap and cheers.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Listen guys," Bra Steve says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must stand together to fight against gender-based violence and femicide." Bra Steve is the local organiser of Father A Nation, a non-profit that works with men and boys to promote positive masculinity and help end violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group's meeting comes as South Africa grapples with renewed anger over renewed cases of femicide and violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Bra Steve says: "We must restore dignity to the men around here" South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged that his government has not done enough and announced measures he hopes can make women feel safer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: A report in 2022 by the Human Sciences Research Council found that more than 35% of South African women experienced physical or sexual violence, many from their own intimate partners.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: For Bra Steve, part of the solution to the crisis is helping men to understand the issue and take responsibility for their actions.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are a lost generation," he says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must restore dignity to the men around here." Amongst the group of men outside the tavern is Zizipho Mtwesi, the project co-ordinator of Father A Nation.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Reflecting on recent weeks, he says more should be done.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The latest measures announced by Ramaphosa, including better street lighting and a review of unsolved cases , are too little, he says, and too late.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "When I think about all of these recent murders in Johannesburg, I get angry.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Why do we have to wait for this to happen for us to act?" He looks around and gestures at the meeting.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are trying to reach men before things like these murders happen again." Craig Wilkinson tells the group to "choose what kind of man you want to be" Craig Wilkinson is the founder of the group.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We get men to talk, to process their feelings," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "And as they do, this healing takes place.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: And the second phase is teaching and training positive masculinity.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We ultimately hope that this will eliminate the scourge of gender-based violence." He stands up, moving into the centre of the group, calling out to the men.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "You as a man are a powerful force for good," he tells them.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "You choose what kind of man you want to be.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Women need to be safe." Father A Nation operates across South Africa, teaching healthy masculinity and running training programmes across dozens of schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Mystery surrounds the spate of murders which has sparked South Africa's latest moment of soul-searching about the safety of its women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Police have not ruled out potential links between some of the Ekurhuleni deaths but have not said they are investigating a serial killer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Suspects in some of the cases have appeared in court.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: But the spate of deaths has sparked new concerns and in Organic Market some women are more fearful than ever.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Outside a nearby shack Linkie listens with interest as she cleans clothes in a large metal bucket.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are not safe when we are outside our place," she says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are afraid when we see a car behind us when we walk.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: What if this guy's going to kidnap me or do something to me?" It is a feeling shared by many women here.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In the local hair salon, sporting a mane of thick pink braids, is Providence Maseko.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: She comes to the door to speak to Bra Steve.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: This video can not be played Women held a memorial run in Johannesburg after the discovery of Moselakgomo's body "Safety here is very bad," she says, "Maybe you are the serial killer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: How do I know who to trust?" Bra Steve laughs.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must talk about these things," he urges.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Come to our meetings and we can learn to trust each other." Maseko tells me that she now takes an e-hailing taxi everywhere in the hope that it is safer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Back at the tavern, the men's meeting is wrapping up.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "As we try to stop gender-based violence," says Zizipho, "each and every man needs to know that they need to play a part in this.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "And if they wouldn't allow these things to happen to their own daughters or own mothers, they mustn't allow it to be done to someone else's daughter, which is their wives or their girlfriends." Mathekga is impressed with what he has heard.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "I would love them to keep on practising what we have learned, because we no longer have role models," he says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Our fathers and our uncles, they are there in prison.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: We must now become role models and help make this country better." Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July.

sentences.text: The student journalist turned civic mobiliser launched a voter registration drive on social media earlier this year, using snappy selfies infused with music and humour to target young people.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: The result astonished him and many observers of Kenyan politics – by the time the registration period ended, 2.6 million new voters across the country had signed up.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: He is aiming to get another 2.3 million on board in the next round.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: "It was the Gen Z way of doing politics," he tells me.

sentences.text: "Fun, trendy, sexy, fashionable.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: Because of how we created the hype around it, people had the fear of missing out.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: Everybody wanted to be involved." Gen Z, the term used to describe people born in the late 1990s and early 2000s, burst onto the scene two years ago with mass protests that forced the government to retreat on a widely unpopular tax bill.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: But their victory was followed by a police crackdown that killed and injured dozens of demonstrators.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: And they have the numbers to make a difference - more than 30% of voting-age Kenyans are younger than 35.
sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: Polls suggest President William Ruto is looking vulnerable.

sentences.article_title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election

sentences.text: "These youth-led movements are a wild card, in that they are unpredictable," says political analyst Tom Mboya.

sentences.text: Magicians, jugglers, puppeteers and acrobats once made a living from crowds in public spaces.
